question: Should External macOS desktop support land with the KIN-1284 bearer portal-viewer bootstrap in one release, and what live macOS and upgrade proof is mandatory before merge?
rationale: The implementation introduces substantial configuration, credential, routing, and portal-authentication surface; choosing the permanent bundle boundary or waiving unavailable provider-backed proof requires maintainer product and risk ownership.

options.title: Split and prove External macOS
options.body: Land the narrower External desktop capability only after exact-head real macOS and upgrade proof, with the bearer-viewer bootstrap reviewed separately.

options.title: Keep bundle and require full proof
options.body: Retain the combined branch but block merge until real macOS lifecycle and released-version upgrade evidence covers both credential and viewer-session paths.

options.title: Accept the proof gap
options.body: Merge the combined feature using synthetic and Linux evidence while explicitly owning the remaining macOS compatibility and security-boundary uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Split and prove External macOS
recommendation.body: Land the narrower External desktop capability only after exact-head real macOS and upgrade proof, with the bearer-viewer bootstrap reviewed separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the relevant merged trust and portal foundations and have made the branch's documented scope and proof decisions throughout review.
